summary: Setting up a Linear OAuth 2.0 application requires registering an application in the Linear developer portal and configuring callback URLs. It is straightforward and supports standard OAuth 2.0 flows along with PKCE options. The main catch is that every admin in the managing workspace has access to the application, so creating a dedicated workspace is recommended.

steps.title: Create a Workspace for Managing the OAuth App
steps.detail: Create a separate Linear workspace specifically for managing the OAuth2 application, as all admin users in the workspace will have access to it.

steps.title: Create a New OAuth2 Application
steps.detail: Navigate to the Linear developer portal and create a new OAuth2 application. Configure the authorized redirect callback URIs to get your Client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Configure Authorization Redirect URL and Scopes
steps.detail: Direct users to `https://linear.app/oauth/authorize` passing `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, and `scope` (such as `read`, `issues:create`, `comments:create`, `timeSchedule:write`, or `admin`). PKCE parameters (`code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method`) can also be included.

nuances: It is highly recommended to create a dedicated workspace to manage the OAuth2 application because every admin user in the workspace will have access to the app.
All OAuth2 applications were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026.
Targeted scopes such as `issues:create` or `comments:create` should be used instead of broader scopes whenever possible.
agent_can_do: Format and construct the authorization endpoint URL with appropriate parameters and scopes.
Implement the authorization flow, state checks, PKCE challenge generation, and token exchange.
human_must_do: Create a dedicated Linear workspace for managing the OAuth application.
Register the OAuth2 application in Linear developer settings.
Define and enter redirect callback URIs in the Linear UI.
Retrieve and safely store the generated Client ID and Client Secret.
